text:
Introduce yourself (also at the OET Speaking test)
                                                            Greet patient by name
- Monitor your body language                                Introduce colleague who may be accompanying you
                                                            Enter with a smile
                                                            Make eye contact
                                                            Sit at eye level
                                                            Face the patient
                                                            Respond appropriately to the patient as someone who
                                                            needs your clinical skills


- Practise active listening skills                          Ask patient for clarification
                                                            You may need to paraphrase (repeat using different
                                                            words) important pieces of information
                                                            Nod your head to encourage patient to keep talking
                                                            If at all possible, don’t interrupt the exchange of
                                                            information to take phone calls


- Be culturally sensitive
                                                            Don’t expect to shake hands with Islamic women – who
                                                            may find this offensive
                                                            Some cultures find it very offensive for females (and
                                                            males) to be scantily clad in hot weather – think about
                                                            your dress code
                                                            In some cultures, “sitting next to” someone might mean
                                                            being no closer than one metre away!


- Be empathic, compassionate, trustworthy
                                                            Treat patients as your equal: everyone has something to
                                                            contribute
                                                            Be open about taking notes – remind the patient that
                                                            patient notes are kept under lock and key and private
                                                            details are not revealed to anyone
                                                            Don’t ever say: ‘You must do ….” “You will have to …” but
                                                            rather “I strongly suggest ..” “I strong urge you to ..”
Practise the RESPECT model

Rapport          Establish a relationship with the patient / find something you have in common (both like movies)
Empathy          You can put yourself in your patient’s shoes – you understand how they must feel
Support          You are a supportive link to a better healthier life
Partnership      Not a legally-binding partnership, but an emotional one with the joint purpose of achieving good
                  health
Explanations Use easy-to-understand “layman” language – not professional jargon; keep it as simple as possible.
Cultural competence You are proud of your cultural heritage and respectful of your patient’s
Trust         Engender trust between you and your patient by being clear and “upfront” in your interactions
